> 277	  let max: number | null = null;
> 278	  const re = /YAVG=([-\d.]+)/g;
> 279	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
> 280	  while ((m = re.exec(text)) !== null) {
> 281	    const v = Number.parseFloat(m[1]);
> 282	    if (Number.isFinite(v)) max = max === null ? v : Math.max(max, v);
> 283	  }
> 284	  return max;
> 285	}
> 286	
> 287	/** Deterministic sample instants across the cut: start / mid / end (end nudged just inside the window).
> 288	 * Exported so the face-detect pre-pass (Fatia 2) can sample the EXACT same instants this picker scores. */
> 289	export function sampleTimes(inSec: number, outSec: number, count: number): number[] {
> 290	  const start = Math.max(0, Number.isFinite(inSec) ? inSec : 0);
> 291	  const end = Math.max(start, Number.isFinite(outSec) ? outSec : start);
> 292	  const span = end - start;
> 293	  if (span <= 0.3 || count <= 1) return [start];
> 294	  const nudge = Math.min(0.1, span * 0.05);
> 295	  const mid = start + span / 2;
> 296	  const last = Math.max(start, end - nudge);
> 297	  const all = count >= 3 ? [start, mid, last] : [start, last];
> 298	  // Dedupe near-identical instants (a tiny window can collapse mid/last onto the endpoints).
> 299	  const out: number[] = [];
> 300	  for (const t of all) if (!out.some((u) => Math.abs(u - t) < 0.02)) out.push(t);
> 301	  return out;
> 302	}
> 303	
> 304	/** The fail-open default result — deterministic, unmeasured, never throws. */
> 305	function defaultPick(elapsedMs: number): ZonePick {
> 306	  const scores: ZoneScore[] = PREFERENCE.map((zone) => ({ zone, agitation: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, rect: ZONE_RECTS[zone] }));

> 308	}
> 309	
> 310	/**
> 311	 * Pick the calmest zone for the motion-graphics card over the cut window [in_sec, out_sec].
> 312	 *
> 313	 * Fail-open contract: NEVER throws. On any FFmpeg/source failure (or insufficient readings) it returns the
> 314	 * deterministic `lower-left` default with `degraded:true`. Zone choice is cosmetic — it must never break a render.
> 315	 */
> 316	export async function pickCalmestZone(
> 317	  sourcePath: string,
> 318	  inSec: number,
> 319	  outSec: number,
> 320	  opts: ZoneSaliencyOptions = {},
> 321	): Promise<ZonePick> {
> 322	  const t0 = performance.now();
> 323	  const workW = Math.max(2, Math.floor(opts.workW ?? 540));
> 324	  const workH = Math.max(2, Math.floor(opts.workH ?? 960));
> 325	  const aspect = opts.aspect && opts.aspect > 0 ? opts.aspect : 9 / 16;
> 326	  const sampleCount = Math.min(3, Math.max(1, Math.floor(opts.sampleCount ?? 3)));
> 327	  const ffmpegPath = opts.ffmpegPath ?? 'ffmpeg';
> 328	
> 329	  if (!existsSync(sourcePath)) return defaultPick(performance.now() - t0);
> 330	
> 331	  const times = sampleTimes(inSec, outSec, sampleCount);
> 332	  // Per-zone temporal MAX of agitation — the worst instant governs so the card never lands where the footage
> 333	  // is briefly busy. Undefined until a zone gets at least one reading.
> 334	  const maxAgitation = {} as Partial<Record<Zone, number>>;
> 335	  let metaDir: string | null = null;
> 336	  try {
> 337	    metaDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'zone-saliency-'));
> 338	    for (let s = 0; s < times.length; s++) {
> 339	      const { args, files } = buildPassArgs(ffmpegPath, sourcePath, times[s], workW, workH, aspect, metaDir, s);
> 340	      const res = await runFfmpeg(ffmpegPath, args);
> 341	      if (res.code !== 0) continue; // fail-soft per instant; other instants may still succeed
> 342	      for (const zone of ZONE_ORDER) {
> 343	        const v = readYavg(files[zone]);
> 344	        if (v === null) continue;
> 345	        const prev = maxAgitation[zone];
> 346	        maxAgitation[zone] = prev === undefined ? v : Math.max(prev, v);
> 347	      }
> 348	    }
> 349	  } catch {
> 350	    return defaultPick(performance.now() - t0);
> 351	  } finally {
> 352	    if (metaDir) rmSync(metaDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
> 353	  }
> 354	
> 355	  // Only zones that (a) got a reading and (b) fit the card minimum are selectable.
> 356	  const selectable = ZONE_ORDER.filter((z) => maxAgitation[z] !== undefined && zoneFits(z));
> 357	  if (selectable.length === 0) return defaultPick(performance.now() - t0);
> 358	
> 359	  // ── Fatia 2 (OTD-VR-016): face-forbidden exclusion ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> 360	  // Steer text off the subject. Absent/empty `forbidden` ⇒ this whole block is inert and behavior is IDENTICAL
> 361	  // to Fatia 1. Otherwise, drop zones that overlap the face union beyond EXCLUDE_FRAC, then pick the calmest
> 362	  // survivor. If a huge/central face covers EVERY readable zone, never return empty — fall back to the least
> 363	  // face-covered zone (calm as tie-break) and flag `faceExcludedAll` so the operator sees the degraded avoidance.
> 364	  const forbidden = (opts.forbidden ?? []).filter(isUsableForbidden);
> 365	  const overlapOf = (z: Zone): number => zoneFaceOverlap(ZONE_RECTS[z], forbidden);
> 366	
> 367	  let candidates = selectable;
> 368	  let faceExcludedAll = false;
> 369	  if (forbidden.length) {
> 370	    const survivors = selectable.filter((z) => overlapOf(z) <= EXCLUDE_FRAC);
> 371	    if (survivors.length) {
> 372	      candidates = survivors;
> 373	    } else {
> 374	      faceExcludedAll = true; // rank ALL readable zones by least face overlap first (below)
> 375	    }
> 376	  }
> 377	
> 378	  const scores: ZoneScore[] = candidates
> 379	    .map((zone) => ({ zone, agitation: maxAgitation[zone] as number, rect: ZONE_RECTS[zone] }))
> 380	    // Ranking: when the face covers everything, least face-overlap wins first (bucketed); otherwise (and as the
> 381	    // secondary key) calmest first — bucket agitation by CALM_EPS so near-equal calm zones defer to PREFERENCE.
> 382	    .sort((a, b) => {
> 383	      if (faceExcludedAll) {
> 384	        const oa = Math.round(overlapOf(a.zone) / OVERLAP_EPS);
> 385	        const ob = Math.round(overlapOf(b.zone) / OVERLAP_EPS);
> 386	        if (oa !== ob) return oa - ob;
> 387	      }
> 388	      const ba = Math.round(a.agitation / CALM_EPS);
> 389	      const bb = Math.round(b.agitation / CALM_EPS);
> 390	      if (ba !== bb) return ba - bb;
> 391	      return PREF_INDEX[a.zone] - PREF_INDEX[b.zone];
> 392	    });
> 393	
> 394	  const chosen = scores[0].zone;
> 395	  return {
> 396	    zone: chosen,
> 397	    rect: ZONE_RECTS[chosen],
> 398	    scores,
> 399	    degraded: false,
> 400	    faceExcludedAll,
> 401	    elapsedMs: performance.now() - t0,
> 402	  };
> 403	}
> 404	
> ```

> 21	## Why the whole runtime is vendored (not just the model)
> 22	
> 23	The design SSOT (Amendment 12 / OTD-VR-016) noted the `.tflite` as the "only new asset" **because it assumed
> 24	`@mediapipe/tasks-vision` was an authoritative `node_modules` dependency**. It is **not**: `package.json`
> 25	declares `@mediapipe/camera_utils`, `drawing_utils`, and `hands`, but **not** `tasks-vision`. It is only
> 26	transitively present. A plain `npm ci` / `bun install` would therefore **not** restore it, and the detector
> 27	would silently fail-open to Fatia 1 forever — an invisible regression. Vendoring the small bundle (~140 KB) +
> 28	the SIMD WASM (~9.7 MB) makes the feature **version-independent and genuinely self-contained** (Law 1 —
> 29	robustness over an undeclared transitive dependency). The ~10 MB one-time git cost buys an air-gapped,

> 32	**SIMD only:** headless Chromium (the exact Playwright build the render pipeline pins) supports WASM SIMD, so
> 33	only the SIMD variant is shipped. If a future host ever lacks SIMD, `FilesetResolver` fails to load the
> 34	runtime → `detectFaceRegions` **fails open** (returns `[]`, `degraded:true`) → placement degrades to the
> 35	Fatia 1 calm-zone behavior. Never a crash.

Now I'm pushing harder to find genuine defects rather than just confirming the code is careful—let me look more aggressively at potential issues, starting with what happens in `ensureDetectorPage` if the page fails to load.

The browser connection check only verifies the browser is still connected, not whether the page itself has crashed. If the page dies while the browser stays alive, we'd return a dead page object, causing `page.evaluate` to throw an error that gets caught and continues with zero samples, triggering degradation. It's a fail-open scenario that's not fatal since the error handling catches it, though checking `!_page.isClosed()` would be more robust. I'm also noticing the route handler might be capturing non-HTTP URLs like `about:blank` and `chrome://` errors in the blocked requests list, which could be worth examining more closely.

Looking at the concurrency angle — `detectFaceRegions` is only called from segment-core which runs sequentially, so the cached page isn't being accessed in parallel. That's not a concern. The one real issue I'm seeing is that `_blockedNetworkRequests` could grow unbounded over time, though in practice it seems manageable. Adding a simple length guard to the push operation is trivial and safe—it preserves the smoke test's semantics while preventing unbounded growth, so I'll implement that one-line change and move forward.

But I should verify whether the long-lived worker actually reuses the browser process across clips, and if so, whether the cached page's route handler could be leaking memory. Not a critical issue. After thorough adversarial and security review with real face detection validation and full test coverage, I haven't found any load-bearing security or correctness defects—the security posture holds up across all the attack vectors I examined. I'll apply one defensive hardening to bound the unbounded telemetry logging and then wrap up my findings.

Let me think through the fix carefully. The smoke tests call `getBlockedNetworkRequests()` and check if the length equals zero, so bounding the buffer only affects cases where it would exceed the cap anyway. The zero-length path stays unaffected, and the telemetry signal for "was anything blocked" is preserved. It's safe to implement.

I'll add this with a named constant and clear documentation, then decide whether to reset the buffer per-request or keep it as-is.

## 🤖 Claude *(21:25:40)*

Adversarial + security review of Fatia 2 (face detection) complete, with material proof on every axis. My slice: `scripts/video-repurpose/face-detect.ts`, `zone-saliency.ts` (Fatia 2 exclusion block), `segment-core.ts` (face wiring), `face-assets/`, `scripts/qa/smoke-face-aware-zone.ts`.

## Veredito de segurança (os 5 eixos caçados)

**1. Command injection — LIMPO.** Todo spawn usa ARRAY, nunca string de shell:
- `face-detect.ts:229` `spawn(ffmpegPath, args, …)`; args montado em `extractReframedFrame:218-225`.
- `zone-saliency.ts:223` `spawn(cmd, args, …)`; args em `buildPassArgs:262-268`.
- `sourcePath` (dado do caller) vem **depois de `-i`** em ambos (`face-detect.ts:222`, `zone-saliency.ts:265`), então um path com `-` inicial vira o *valor* de `-i` (nome de arquivo), não uma nova opção do ffmpeg. As expressões de crop/reframe carregam só frações fixas (`min(iw\,ih*${aspect})`, `iw*${r.w}`) — nenhum dado do caller interpolado no filtergraph. Inerte.

**2. Rede em runtime — LIMPO, air-gapped por construção e PROVADO.** O detector carrega tudo de disco via `file://` relativo (`detector.html:19,32,35`): bundle ESM, WASM (`FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks('./wasm')`), modelo `.tflite`. Varredura do bundle: nenhuma URL http/https; a única string `googleapis` é um *type-URL* de protobuf (`type.googleapis.com/mediapipe…`), não um endpoint buscado. O glue WASM resolve por `scriptDirectory`/`locateFile` (local). Além disso, `page.route('**/*')` (`face-detect.ts:163-168`) ABORTA qualquer coisa que não seja `file://`/`data:`/`blob:` — defesa em profundidade. **Prova material (rodado agora):** G6 detectou rosto real com `blockedNetworkRequests = []` (nenhuma requisição de rede foi necessária).

**3. Path traversal — LIMPO.** Assets do detector por caminho FIXO (`face-detect.ts:51-55`, `join(__dirname,'face-assets',…)`) — nenhuma string do caller. Os frames passados ao browser são temp internos (`mkdtempSync` + `f_${sampled}.png`), nunca caminho do caller.

**4. Fail-open logado — LIMPO.** `ensureDetectorPage` catch → `console.warn` (`:174`); `detectFaceRegions` catch externo → `console.warn` (`:344`); eval por-frame → `console.warn` (`:316`); assets ausentes → `console.warn` (`:290`). A degradação da escolha de zona é logada no nível do clipe em `segment-core.ts` (`face-detect degraded`, `zone-saliency degraded`, `faceExcludedAll`). Sem catch vazio silencioso no caminho observável.

**5. Regressão / Fatia 1 intacta — LIMPO e PROVADO.** `pickCalmestZone` sem `forbidden`: o bloco Fatia 2 (`zone-saliency.ts:369`) é pulado (`if (forbidden.length)`) e o sort ignora overlap (`faceExcludedAll` false) → **idêntico** a hoje. Os 7 estilos de legenda NÃO chamam o detector — tudo é gated por `style === MOTION_GRAPHICS_STYLE` (`segment-core.ts`). Default (`caption_style` undefined → `viral-caption-overlay-9x16`) não entra no bloco. Provado por: smoke-face-aware G3 (`scores=6`, not degraded) + smoke-zone-saliency G1-G4 verde.

## Prova material (Lei 1 — OCULAR + geométrica)
Rodei `smoke-face-aware-zone.ts` no rosto REAL `/home/ubuntu/final.mp4`: 3 frames amostrados, offline, bbox mesclada `frac(x=0.630, y=0.294, w=0.370, h=0.228)`. Extraí o frame reframado (mesmo center-crop 9:16 do render) com essa bbox desenhada e **inspecionei visualmente**: o retângulo cai SOBRE o rosto (olhos/nariz/boca do sujeito de perfil à direita), não no vazio. Contrato geométrico verificado: os três reframes são idênticos (`crop=min(iw,ih*ar):min(ih,iw/ar):(iw-ow)/2:(ih-oh)/2,scale…,crop…,setsar=1` em `face-detect.ts:208-212`, `zone-saliency.ts:211-215`, `segment-core.ts:106`) e o overlay é `overlay=0:0`. A zona escolhida foi upper-left (`overlap=0.000`) — texto desviado do sujeito.

- tsc: limpo nos arquivos da fatia. O único erro (`import.meta.main` em `render-core.ts:568`) é um bun-ism pré-existente em arquivo FORA da fatia, artefato do meu tsc isolado sem `bun-types` (os 2 smokes rodaram sob bun com exit 0, prova mais forte).
- `bun run test`: **648 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed** (exit 0).

## Defeito corrigido (dentro da fatia)
`scripts/video-repurpose/face-detect.ts` — buffer-testemunha de air-gap `_blockedNetworkRequests` era um array global de processo, sem limite (linha ~112), `push` incondicional na rota de abort (linha ~166). Severidade baixa (fica vazio no caminho feliz), mas no worker systemd de vida longa (browser+page cacheados por todo o processo) um asset defeituoso em loop de requisições cresceria isso sem limite. **Correção:** constante `MAX_BLOCKED_LOG = 64` + guarda `if (_blockedNetworkRequests.length < MAX_BLOCKED_LOG) push`. Transparente a todo consumidor (o smoke assere `length === 0`; qualquer buffer não-vazio já prova violação). Re-rodei o smoke pós-fix: G6 verde, `blockedNetworkRequests = []`, SMOKE PASS.

## Aberto para o Sovereign (não-bloqueante, nenhum é defeito de segurança)
- **Limite conhecido e honesto (já documentado no header de `face-detect.ts:34-36`):** blaze_face_short_range é frontal/near-frontal — perfil fechado, oclusão pesada ou rosto minúsculo pode ser PERDIDO; nesse caso a placagem cai em Fatia 1 (calma) para aquele instante. É refino, não garantia. Aceito por design (fail-open).
- **Erro aspecto ~0,08%:** frame de análise do detector é 608×1080 (0,56296) vs 9:16 exato (0,5625); distorção horizontal < 1px na fração — imaterial para exclusão grosseira de região. Não corrigido (não vale o risco de mexer no tamanho "provado").
- **`closeFaceDetector()` não é chamado no shutdown do `video-repurpose-bridge.ts`** — o browser cacheado é reaproveitado entre clipes (perf, correto) e reapado pelo `process.once('exit')`. Encaixar `closeFaceDetector` no SIGTERM do worker é nice-to-have, não defeito.
- **`ensureDetectorPage` (`:135`) checa `_browser.isConnected()` mas não `_page.isClosed()`** — se a page morrer com o browser vivo, `page.evaluate` lança → é capturado → `continue` → `degrade()`. Fail-open correto; endurecer com `!_page.isClosed()` é cosmético.
